Interactive, stdin, daemon, WebSocket, or ACP — one engine, one config. A supervising model plans and checks the work. Policy lives in TOML guardrails, not approval prompts. Website · Docs · Tap Registry · Benchmarks · Issues Octomind is an open-source coding agent harness. It gives an LLM real access to your repo — reading and writing files, running shells, searching code, delegating to sub-agents — through MCP tools. The same harness runs interactively , non-interactively through stdin , as a background daemon , over WebSocket , or as an ACP agent inside your editor or another agent's stack. # Interactive octomind run developer:general # Piped — CI, scripts, automation echo " Explain the auth module " | octomind run developer:general --format plain # Daemon — keep it alive, talk to it from another terminal echo " watch the build " | octomind run --name watcher --daemon --format jsonl octomind send --name watcher " run the test suite " Why Octomind? Most coding agents assume a human is watching the screen. Octomind is built for the work that keeps going after you leave. 1. Install (macOS, Linux): curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muvon/octomind/master/install.sh | bash On Windows, in PowerShell: irm https: // raw.githubusercontent.com / muvon / octomind / master / install.ps1 | iex On macOS, you can also install with Homebrew: brew install muvon/tap/octomind 2. Get model access. The fastest path is Octomind Cloud, which includes models and needs no configuration: octomind login Prefer your own provider key? Skip login and export one (also OPENAI_API_KEY , ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ), then follow Model access to point the config at it: export OPENROUTER_API_KEY= " your_key " 3. Run a specialist in your project: cd ~ /your/project octomind run developer:general You're now in a session with an agent that can read your code, run commands, and edit files. The interface is a plain line prompt with markdown rendering — no TUI to learn, so it works over SSH, in tmux , and in CI logs. The first time you run a specialist, it may install its tools and ask for credentials. developer:general comes from the default tap muvon/tap , not your local config. Plain octomind run starts the config's default role, assistant:concierge . Try the recorded bug-fix demo : two failing tests, an agent fix, and an independent test rerun. Measured on octobench against 25 tasks harvested from merged pull requests across Python, PHP, Rust, C++, and JavaScript. Each agent works in the pre-fix repo; held-out tests from the merged fix decide pass or fail. These are the published July 30, 2026 results, not a measurement of this checkout. Drop a .agents/guardrails.toml in your repo. Octomind enforces it deterministically, with no code to compile and no plugin to install. # Pre-call deny — block a class of calls before they execute [[ guard ]] match = " shell(command=^rm \\ s+-rf?) " message = " rm -rf blocked. " # Conditional rule — only fires after the agent ran git status this session [[ guard ]] match = " shell(command=git push) " when = [ " +shell(command=git status) " ] message = " Review changes before pushing. " Layer When it runs What it does Guards Before a tool call Deny by capability, argument regex, and session history. A match returns a denial instead of executing the call. Hooks After a tool result A non-zero exit injects stdout into the agent's inbox — lint and format failures become automatic corrections without restarting the turn. Validators After a turn Scripts the agent reads on its next turn. This replaces "approve this change?" prompts in autonomous loops. If you know Claude Code hooks: guards are PreToolUse denies declared in TOML, hooks are PostToolUse , validators are Stop — no scripts required for the common cases. Hook and validator script examples: Guardrails guide . The same harness, exposed wherever your workflow needs it. Need machine-readable results? Pass --schema schema.json to constrain the final response to a JSON Schema (requires a model with structured-output support). See Structured output . octomind run developer:general # general dev, language skills auto-activate octomind run doctor:blood # blood-test interpretation specialist octomind run lawyer:sg # legal specialist Running a specialist fetches its manifest from the tap registry, installs any required binaries, resolves credentials, starts the right MCP servers, and then opens the session. Build and register your own: octomind tap init yourteam/my-tap # scaffold, validate, git-init, and register locally octomind tap yourteam/my-tap # on another machine, after publishing to GitHub The octomind- prefix is added automatically: yourteam/my-tap maps to the repository yourteam/octomind-my-tap . The install script detects your OS and architecture (Linux and macOS on x86_64/aarch64) and installs to ~/.local/bin/ . Pass --install-dir <DIR> or set OCTOMIND_INSTALL_DIR to override. On Windows (x86_64/aarch64), install.ps1 installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\octomind\bin and adds it to your user PATH ; it honors OCTOMIND_INSTALL_DIR and OCTOMIND_VERSION too. install.sh still works from Git Bash or MSYS2. Command not found? Add the install directory to your PATH : export PATH= " $HOME /.local/bin: $PATH " Building from source requires protoc ; see Building from source for per-OS prerequisites. Verify: octomind --version octomind config # generate the default config octomind run # start your first session Shell completions: octomind completion <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell> . Octomind Cloud — octomind login (device-code sign-in, like gh auth login ) stores a gateway key locally. The default config already uses octohub:auto . Learn more . Bring your own key — set the provider's environment variable ( OPENROUTER_API_KEY , OPENAI_API_KEY , ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , DEEPSEEK_API_KEY , …) and point the model tables at it. The supervisor and compression profiles also default to octohub:auto , so update all three: [ model ] name = " anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5 " [ supervisor . model ] name = " anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5 " [ compression . model ] name = " anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5 " Provider details and per-role overrides: Providers & models . Config lives at ~/.local/share/octomind/config/config.toml on macOS and Linux, and under %LOCALAPPDATA%/octomind/config/ on Windows. Set OCTOMIND_DATA_DIR to override the data root. octomind config --show # view current config octomind config --validate # validate config Override any value for a single run with -c : octomind run -c supervisor.enabled=false Full reference: Configuration reference · Environment variables . Full list: Session commands . Octomind reports anonymous usage: which commands, tools, and models are used, plus timings, token counts, and error kinds. It never sends your code, prompts, file paths, tool arguments, or environment values. Opt out in any of three ways: export DO_NOT_TRACK=1 # the cross-tool standard, honored first export OCTOMIND_TELEMETRY=0 # for subsequent commands in this shell # or set `telemetry = false` in config.toml Exact field list: Telemetry .
